craft.name: James Webb Space Telescope
craft.blurb: The largest telescope ever flown: a 6.5 m gold-coated mirror kept at −233 °C behind a sunshield the size of a tennis court. It circles the L2 point, 1.5 million km beyond the Earth.

craft.name: Euclid
craft.blurb: Maps the shapes and distances of billions of galaxies across a third of the sky to learn how dark matter and dark energy have shaped the universe.

craft.name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
craft.blurb: A mirror the size of Hubble's with a field of view a hundred times wider, built to survey dark energy and to find planets by the way their gravity bends starlight.

craft.name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory
craft.blurb: Has stared at the Sun without a break since 1996 and, almost by accident, discovered more than five thousand comets.

craft.name: Deep Space Climate Observatory
craft.blurb: Gives up to an hour's warning of solar storms, and photographs the whole sunlit face of the Earth every couple of hours.

craft.name: Advanced Composition Explorer
craft.blurb: Samples the particles streaming from the Sun and from between the stars; its readings have fed space-weather forecasts since 1998.

craft.name: Wind
craft.blurb: A spinning drum of instruments measuring the solar wind before it reaches the Earth, still at work after more than thirty years.

craft.name: Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe
craft.blurb: Spins four times a minute to map the edge of the Sun's bubble in space, using atoms that drift in from beyond it.

craft.name: Carruthers Geocorona Observatory
craft.role: Ultraviolet camera watching the Earth's outermost atmosphere
craft.blurb: Looks back from L1 at the faint ultraviolet glow of hydrogen that surrounds the Earth out to beyond the Moon.

craft.name: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite
craft.blurb: Watches the nearest stars for the tiny dips of planets crossing them, from a long orbit that goes round twice for every circuit of the Moon.

craft.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
craft.blurb: Has photographed nearly the whole Moon sharply enough to show the Apollo landers and the astronauts' footpaths.

craft.name: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
craft.blurb: India's second lunar mission: its lander was lost, but the orbiter has mapped the Moon and its water ice from a polar orbit ever since.

craft.name: Danuri (Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter)
craft.blurb: South Korea's first craft beyond Earth orbit; one of its cameras can see inside the Moon's permanently shadowed craters.

craft.name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
craft.blurb: The longest-serving spacecraft at another planet: it found buried water ice and has relayed most of what the rovers have sent home.

craft.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
craft.blurb: Carries the largest telescope sent to another planet; it can pick out a rover and its tracks from 300 km up.

craft.name: Mars Express
craft.blurb: Europe's first planetary mission, on a long looping orbit that also takes it close past the moon Phobos.

craft.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
craft.blurb: Sniffs the Martian air for gases such as methane at a few parts in a trillion, and passes on data from the rovers below.

craft.name: Emirates Mars Mission (Hope)
craft.blurb: The first Arab mission to another planet, on a high orbit from which it sees a whole hemisphere of Martian weather at a time.

craft.name: Curiosity (Mars Science Laboratory)
craft.blurb: A car-sized, nuclear-powered rover that has been climbing Mount Sharp in Gale crater since 2012, reading the layers of an ancient lake bed.

craft.name: Perseverance (Mars 2020)
craft.blurb: Collects rock cores in and around Jezero crater, once a river delta, for a later mission to bring back; it carried the helicopter Ingenuity.

craft.name: InSight
craft.blurb: Listened to more than 1,300 marsquakes and measured the size of the planet's core before dust on its solar panels ended the mission in December 2022.

craft.name: Zhurong (Tianwen-1 rover)
craft.blurb: China's first Mars rover drove nearly two kilometres across Utopia Planitia; it went into hibernation for the winter of 2022 and has not woken.

craft.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
craft.blurb: The first fully successful commercial Moon landing: it worked in Mare Crisium for a whole lunar day in March 2025 and filmed a sunset there.

craft.name: Odysseus (IM-1)
craft.blurb: The first American landing on the Moon since Apollo 17; it came down near the south pole in February 2024, tipped onto its side and still sent data for six days.

craft.name: Chandrayaan-3 lander (Vikram)
craft.blurb: Made India the fourth country to land on the Moon, in August 2023, and the first near its south pole; the small rover Pragyan drove off its ramp.

craft.name: SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon)
craft.blurb: Japan's "Moon Sniper" landed within 55 m of its target in January 2024, ended up on its nose, and still survived three lunar nights.

craft.name: Juno
craft.blurb: A spinning, solar-powered craft on a long orbit over Jupiter's poles; each close pass skims the cloud tops at 200,000 km/h.

craft.name: Europa Clipper
craft.blurb: The largest planetary spacecraft NASA has built, due at Jupiter in 2030 to fly past Europa about fifty times and learn whether its ocean could support life.

craft.name: Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer
craft.role: Jupiter moons explorer, on its way
craft.blurb: Due at Jupiter in 2031 to study Europa, Callisto and above all Ganymede, where it is to become the first craft to orbit a moon of another planet.

craft.name: BepiColombo
craft.blurb: Two orbiters, one European and one Japanese, travelling as a single stack; after nine fly-bys of the Earth, Venus and Mercury they arrive at Mercury in late 2026.

craft.name: Lucy
craft.blurb: On a twelve-year tour of the Trojans, the asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit and have hardly changed since the planets formed.

craft.name: Psyche
craft.blurb: Flying on ion engines to the asteroid 16 Psyche, which may be the exposed iron core of a world that never finished forming; it arrives in 2029.

craft.name: OSIRIS-APEX
craft.blurb: As OSIRIS-REx it brought home 121 g of the asteroid Bennu in 2023; renamed, it is heading for Apophis, to arrive just after that asteroid's close pass of the Earth in 2029.

craft.name: Hayabusa2
craft.blurb: Delivered pieces of the asteroid Ryugu to the Earth in 2020 and flew on; its extended mission is to reach a small, fast-spinning asteroid in 2031.

craft.name: Hera
craft.blurb: Sent to the double asteroid Didymos, which it was due to reach in late 2026, to measure the crater and the change of orbit left when NASA's DART deliberately hit its small moon in 2022.

craft.name: Martian Moons eXploration
craft.role: Phobos sample-return mission, on its way
craft.blurb: Due at Mars in 2027 to land on its moon Phobos, collect at least ten grams of the surface and bring them back to the Earth in 2031.

craft.name: Parker Solar Probe
craft.blurb: The fastest object people have made: it dives to within 6.1 million km of the Sun's surface at 690,000 km/h, through the Sun's own atmosphere.

craft.name: Solar Orbiter
craft.blurb: Photographs the Sun from inside Mercury's orbit and is tilting its own orbit, pass by pass, to give the first clear views of the Sun's poles.

craft.name: STEREO-A
craft.blurb: Orbits the Sun slightly faster than the Earth, so it sees solar storms from an angle no telescope near the Earth can.

craft.name: BioSentinel
craft.blurb: A satellite the size of a cereal box that rode along with Artemis I and now measures the radiation of deep space from its own orbit round the Sun.

craft.name: Voyager 1
craft.blurb: The most distant thing people have made. It passed Jupiter and Saturn, crossed into interstellar space in 2012 and still answers, on a signal that takes about a day to arrive.

craft.name: Voyager 2
craft.blurb: The only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune; it followed its twin into interstellar space in 2018.

craft.name: New Horizons
craft.blurb: Flew past Pluto in 2015 and the small world Arrokoth in 2019, and is now crossing the Kuiper belt on its way out of the solar system.

craft.name: Pioneer 10
craft.blurb: The first craft through the asteroid belt and past Jupiter. Its last faint signal was heard in January 2003; it coasts on towards the star Aldebaran.

craft.name: Pioneer 11
craft.blurb: Used Jupiter's gravity to become the first craft to reach Saturn, in 1979. Contact ended in 1995.

craft.name: Gaia
craft.blurb: Measured the positions and motions of nearly two billion stars from L2. Out of fuel, it was moved to an orbit round the Sun and switched off in March 2025.

craft.name: Kepler space telescope
craft.blurb: Found more than 2,600 planets round other stars by staring at one patch of sky. It ran out of fuel in 2018 and trails the Earth round the Sun.

craft.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
craft.blurb: NASA's infrared Great Observatory worked for sixteen years, drifting ever further behind the Earth, until it was switched off in January 2020.

craft.name: Ulysses
craft.blurb: Used Jupiter to swing out of the plane of the planets and pass over the Sun's poles three times; it fell silent in 2009 and is still on that tilted orbit.

craft.name: Dawn
craft.blurb: The only craft to have orbited two worlds beyond the Earth, Vesta and then Ceres. Its fuel ran out in 2018; it will circle Ceres for decades yet.

craft.name: SpaceX Roadster ("Starman")
craft.role: A car, launched as a test payload
craft.blurb: The dummy cargo of the first Falcon Heavy: a sports car with a spacesuited mannequin at the wheel, on an orbit that reaches out past Mars. It was never able to send anything back.
